title: First-Response Cadre Playbook and CSR Status Lattice
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes the role, responsibilities and procedures for the "First-Response Cadre" (FRC) — the set of people who take immediate action for service signals before the full incident bridge is established. The goal is fast containment, evidence capture, and clear handoff to the incident bridge or service steward. This doc also includes a structured lattice of customer status templates (CSR templates) for common impact tiers.

Audience: oncall engineers, bridge operators, CSRs, SRE leads.

Key objectives
- Acknowledge and classify alerts within 2 minutes for P0/P1 signals.
- Contain customer-visible impact within 30 minutes when possible.
- Preserve forensic evidence (logs, traces, KV snapshots) before remediation alters state.
- Provide consistent customer-facing status lines using the CSR lattice below.

Roles and contacts
1) First Responder (FR) — primary oncall engineer who opened the alert.
   - Responsibility: initial triage, short-term containment, evidence snapshot.
   - Contact: #oncall (Slack), PagerDuty: redwood-prod-oncall
2) Bridge Operator (BO) — sets up and runs the bridge if incident escalates.
   - Responsibility: run the timeline, coordinate cross-team ops.
   - Contact: #bridge-ops
3) Service Steward (SS) — owner of the failing service.
   - Responsibility: hold long-running remediations, postmortem lead.
4) CSR Liaison — customer success liaison for customer-facing comms.
   - Responsibility: select and publish CSR template, route customer questions.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Signal arrival
   - Monitor/alerting systems: Prometheus Alertmanager, Sentinels (latency monitors), LogAnvil (error spikes).
   - FR acknowledges in PagerDuty within 2 minutes.
2. Rapid Triage (0–10 minutes)
   - Determine scope: single region vs global; single-customer vs multi-tenant.
   - Quick checks: deployment events, recent model rollouts, autoscaling events, or noisy neighbors.
   - Evidence capture checklist (run immediately):
     a) Dump top 200 error traces: curl -s "https://loganvil/api/v1/query?service=...&top=200" > evidence/traces-$(date +%s).json
     b) Snapshot KV cache metrics (hit/miss rates) and TTL distributions.
     c) Record in-bridge timeline: timestamp, FR name, hypothesis.
3. Containment (10–30 minutes)
   - Apply short-term mitigations: route traffic to fallback model, disable new rollouts, scale up inferencers, toggle prefix caching.
   - If containment succeeds, mark status as "stabilized" and proceed to incident creation in the bridge if required.
4. Bridge & Escalation (30+ minutes or immediate for P0)
   - BO establishes bridge using template: conference link, triage doc, runbook links, and customer comm ID.
   - Assign action owners and target SLAs for restoration steps.
5. Recovery & Validation
   - Verify steady-state across regions and tenants for at least two 5-minute windows.
6. Postmortem
   - SS leads the write-up within 72 hours; postmortem must include timeline, root cause, action items, and regression tests.

Triage decision ladder (condensed)
- If 95th percentile latency > 2x SLO across >10% of hosts -> escalate to P1.
- If sustained error-rate > 3% for requests over 10 minutes OR confirmed data loss affecting customers -> P0.
- If single-tenant impact and rate-limited -> P2 (service owner to coordinate).

Sample Runbooks (excerpts)
A) KV Cache Eviction Spike
- Trigger: cache eviction rate > 1000 evictions/min and cache hit ratio drops by >15%.
- Steps:
  1) Pause any recent quantization rollouts: infra rollback command.
  2) Temporarily increase cache capacity by 25% for affected shard group: k8s patch.
  3) If autoscaler misbehaving, cascade to manual scale up: runbook/kvs/manual-scale.
  4) Observe 10m; if hit ratio returns above baseline, plan a targeted rollout fix.

B) Model-quality regression (RLHF/eval failure)
- Trigger: quality monitors detect +10% failure rate against golden prompt-set.
- Steps:
  1) Route traffic to previous model version variant with fallback policy.
  2) Open regression ticket and attach evaluation artifacts and seed prompts.
  3) Notify product and research: sr_research@redwood.ai.

On-call rotations, handoffs and etiquette
- Rotation length: 7-day primary oncall blocks with 14-day shadow rotation for junior engineers.
- Handoff checklist (to be posted in Slack at shift change):
  - Confirm no active P0/P1 incidents assigned.
  - Share list of ongoing maintenance windows and scheduled rollouts.
  - Leave brief notes on hotspots (e.g., "KV shard 3 showing elevated GC, watch eviction rate").
- Quiet-window protocol: no major rollouts within primary oncall's first 12 hours unless pre-approved by SRE lead.

Game day design and scoring
- Frequency: quarterly team-wide game days; smaller tabletop run twice monthly for new hires.
- Scenario types: total-threshold outage, progressive degradation (latency oscillation), model-quality regression, cross-region failover.
- Scoring rubric (0–10) per scenario:
  - Detection speed (0–3): time from simulated fault to acknowledged alert.
  - Containment (0–3): mitigation applied correctly within target window.
  - Communication (0–2): customer status + internal bridge notes clarity.
  - After-action (0–2): quality of post-game retro and actionable items.

Postmortem rubric (must-haves)
- Executive summary (1–2 paragraphs)
- Chronological timeline with timestamps and evidence links
- Root cause analysis (5 whys or causal graph)
- Impact and blast radius calculation (tenant list, % of traffic, duration)
- Action items with owners and due dates (no more than 5 high-priority.
- Regressions/test coverage added and verification plan
- Severity classification and whether SLA credits are applicable

SLOs and thresholds (examples)
- Text generation latency SLO: p95 < 300ms (global), p99 < 750ms (regional)
- Error rate SLO: <0.5% (5m rolling) ; Alert if >1% sustained for 5 minutes
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for Redwood API (hosted)

CSR (customer status) lattice (templates)
- Tier A: brief holding message (for initial, uncertain impact)
  Subject: [Redwood] We are investigating degraded service for text-generation
  Body: We are aware of an issue affecting text-generation latency for some customers. Our engineers are investigating. We will provide updates in 30 minutes or sooner. No action required from customers at this time.

- Tier B: intermediate update (confirmed impact, mitigation in progress)
  Subject: [Redwood] Mitigation in progress for reduced throughput
  Body: We have identified a cause for reduced throughput in region us-west-2 and are applying a mitigation. Some requests may receive slower responses or fallbacks to a compatible model. We expect improvement within 60 minutes. If you require assistance, contact support@redwood.ai.

- Tier C: resolved (post-recovery) 
  Subject: [Redwood] Issue resolved — text-generation service restored
  Body: The incident impacting text-generation has been resolved as of 15:24 UTC. We confirmed normal traffic patterns for 30 minutes and will publish a post-incident summary within 72 hours. We apologize for the disruption.

Customer comms templates (CSR examples)
- Short in-incident update (10–30 min cadence):
  "We are continuing to investigate; current mitigation is to route affected requests to the fallback model. Next update in 30 minutes or when there is a material change."

- Escalation / SLA credit notice: include incident ID, duration, affected tenants, and next steps. Use legal@redwood.ai for approvals.

Operational checklists
- Evidence collection checklist (first 15 minutes): traces, sample requests/IDs, model version, deployment id, recent config changes (last 60m), KV cache snapshot.
- Post-incident closure checklist: confirm monitoring stable for 2x SLO window, close incident in PagerDuty, file postmortem draft and schedule review.

Appendix: quick commands & links
- Establish bridge: /tools/bridge/new --template "frc-standard" --service text-generation
- Snapshot logs: curl -s "https://loganvil/api/v1/query?service=text-generation&since=15m" > /tmp/tg-evidence.json
- Rollback model: rdm model rollback --service text-generation --to-version v2026-10-11

Ownership & escalation matrix (summary)
- Level 1 (FR): primary oncall -> #oncall; handles triage and containment.
- Level 2 (BO+SS): bridge operator and service steward -> run bridge and coordinate longer-term mitigations.
- Level 3 (Exec): SRE Director and Product Lead -> invoked for severe multi-customer P0s > 3 hours.
